system_description.narrative_title: US–Iran escalation, Gulf diplomacy and energy-market shock
system_description.narrative_summary: A cycle of threatened U.S. strikes on Iran, last-minute cancellations and regional pressure from Gulf allies is driving acute geopolitical uncertainty. Iran's retaliatory posture and moves to control shipping through Hormuz/Red Sea are disrupting energy flows, prompting OPEC+ adjustments, windfalls for major oil firms and sharp, volatile moves in oil and financial markets.
system_description.scope: Military-diplomatic interactions between the U.S. and Iran; Gulf states' diplomatic and security interventions; disruptions to oil and LNG shipping (Hormuz/Red Sea); OPEC+ production decisions; oil price dynamics, inventories and energy-company earnings; investor sentiment and short-term market reactions.
system_description.super_system: Global political-economy of energy and security (intersection of international security, commodity markets and global finance).
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil & gas markets and trading infrastructure
Middle East regional security architecture and alliances
U.S. domestic politics and presidential decision-making
Maritime shipping, insurance and chokepoint security (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea)
evidence_headlines: Donald Trump cancels new strikes on Iran after Middle East allies’ request
Embassies warn Americans of travel risk amid signs of possible U.S.-Iran military action in the coming days
Oil drops over 4% after Trump calls off planned strike on Iran
Gulf States Pressed Trump to Hold Off on Iran Strikes and Pursue Talks
Chevron and Exxon earnings soar as Trump threatens price interventions
EXCLUSIVE: QatarEnergy buys 33 US LNG cargoes to offset Hormuz disruption, sources say - reuters.com

variables.name: Military escalation threat
variables.description: The intensity of threatened or actual use-of-force actions in the contested military-diplomatic theatre that raise the risk of direct strikes.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement level
variables.description: The volume and intensity of active diplomatic negotiations, shuttle diplomacy and mediating communication among relevant actors.

variables.name: Regional security cooperation
variables.description: The degree of coordination and joint security/activity planning among regional actors around maritime and military issues.

variables.name: Maritime transit disruption rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of incidents, interdictions or threats that disrupt commercial navigation through key maritime chokepoints.

variables.name: Crude supply gap
variables.description: The net reduction in physical crude oil availability to markets relative to normal baseline supply.

variables.name: Production adjustment rate
variables.description: The speed and magnitude at which producing entities change output levels in response to market or policy signals.

variables.name: Global oil inventory level
variables.description: The aggregate stock of crude and refined product inventories held across commercial and strategic stores worldwide.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price of benchmark crude oil that aggregates supply, demand and risk premia.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variability in oil prices reflecting uncertainty and rapid repricing events.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: The average cost rate charged to insure maritime cargoes and tankers transiting contested sea routes.

variables.name: Energy company margin level
variables.description: The aggregate profitability margin across major upstream and integrated energy producers and refiners.

variables.name: Investor risk aversion
variables.description: The prevailing level of investor sensitivity to geopolitical and commodity-market risk that alters portfolio positioning.

variables.name: Financial market liquidity
variables.description: The depth and ease with which financial assets, including energy-sector securities, can be bought or sold without large price impact.

variables.name: Shipping rerouting rate
variables.description: The rate at which commercial voyages are diverted to longer or alternative routes due to security or access constraints.

variables.name: LNG cargo flow rate
variables.description: The throughput rate of liquefied natural gas cargoes moved between producers and buyers, inclusive of re-routing and cargo substitutions.

variables.name: Energy price pass-through rate
variables.description: The speed and extent to which changes in wholesale energy prices transmit to consumer fuel prices and broader inflation measures.

catalysts.title: U.S.–Iran talks resume / negotiation push
catalysts.description: Renewed direct or mediated talks between Washington and Tehran flagged by U.S. statements and Iranian denials — diplomatic engagement likely to pick up in coming days.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump says Iran talks to resume Monday', 'Trump claims Iran talks under way despite denial from Tehran'.

catalysts.title: Saudi-led multinational maritime defence coalition formation
catalysts.description: Saudi Arabia's announced plan to create a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and deter attacks in the Gulf and Red Sea.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Saudi Arabia unveils plans for multinational maritime defence coalition'.

catalysts.title: OPEC+ implementation of September quota increase
catalysts.description: Planned OPEC+ quota increase slated for September, affecting near-term supply flow into markets.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'OPEC+ set for September quota increase', 'OPEC+ agrees September oil hike'.

catalysts.title: QatarEnergy buys 33 US LNG cargoes (increased LNG flows)
catalysts.description: Large QatarEnergy purchases of U.S. LNG cargoes to offset disruptions through Hormuz will boost LNG cargo movements and substitutions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'QatarEnergy buys 33 US LNG cargoes to offset Hormuz disruption, sources say'.

catalysts.title: Iran–Oman shipping-management deal near completion
catalysts.description: Reported close agreement between Iran and Oman to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which could reduce disruptions if finalised.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran says deal with Oman to manage shipping through Hormuz is close'.

catalysts.title: Risk of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran
catalysts.description: Warnings and administration statements signal a non-negligible chance of fresh U.S. military action against Iran in the coming days.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Embassies warn Americans of travel risk amid signs of possible U.S.-Iran military action', 'Trump doubles down on threat to hit Iran'.

catalysts.title: Continued tanker rerouting and detours around dangerous waters
catalysts.description: Ongoing pattern of tankers and cargo ships rerouting around Red Sea/Hormuz and using longer routes in response to attacks and incidents.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Product tanker reroutes around Africa', 'Six Saudi tankers turn away from Gulf of Aden', 'UKMTO reports two tanker incidents off Oman'.

catalysts.title: Iran threats and potential strikes on regional energy infrastructure
catalysts.description: Iranian threats to strike other nations' energy fields if attacked increase the risk of targeted disruptions to production and facilities.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran threatens to strike other nations' energy fields if US launches fresh attacks', 'Iran threatens regional energy fields'.
